questions.q: How do NAV commands differ from DO commands?
options: DO only work on planes and in Rover
NAV is where to fly, DO is what to do
NAV is used only for takeoff
questions.explain: NAV sets where to fly; DO is what to do along the way without changing the route. The mission goes from NAV to NAV.

questions.q: Which altitude frame do you need for a regular mission?
questions.explain: Absolute altitude easily produces an error of hundreds of meters.

options: Where the ground control station is
questions.explain: After relocating, home stays at the old spot — reset it before takeoff.

questions.q: How is a mission uploaded over MAVLink?
options: As a file over a UART port
The aircraft requests waypoints by index
Starts from the first command when entering AUTO
Deletes the mission after the flight ends
questions.explain: By default the mission continues from the current command.

questions.q: Which altitude frame is safe when you change sites?
options: Absolute above sea level from GPS
questions.explain: Absolute altitudes are a classic crash.

Taking a shot every N meters
questions.explain: At the end of the mission — DIST 0.

questions.q: A copter mission is uploaded, but from the ground in Auto the aircraft doesn't take off as expected. What's wrong in the first items?
questions.fragment:
seq cmd                  frame          alt
0   HOME                 GLOBAL         0
1   NAV_WAYPOINT         RELATIVE_ALT   20
2   NAV_WAYPOINT         RELATIVE_ALT   20
3   NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH
options: There's no NAV_TAKEOFF: a copter mission starting from the ground must begin with a takeoff command
Items 1 and 2 have the same altitude, and in Auto a copter requires an altitude change between adjacent mission waypoints
RELATIVE_ALT can't be mixed with HOME in GLOBAL: you need a single frame in all items
NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH at the end is forbidden: a mission must end with NAV_LAND
questions.explain: The first navigation item when starting from the ground is TAKEOFF; that way the behavior is unambiguous.
